# Mermaid does not render in the local dev portal, so every guide's diagram ships unverified

`Serves:` guide authoring — the `guide-authoring` bar requires render-verification of every diagram, and the local portal cannot supply it.

## The Problem

`guide-authoring`'s §3 makes a rendered diagram a merge condition — *"≥1 diagram that carries the story. No-Mermaid = reject"* and *"Render-verify before merge"*. It also concedes the tooling: *"there is no headless renderer locally; route the render-check to a peer with a browser-backed method, or confirm on the portal."*

The local dev portal is not that fallback. A ```` ```mermaid ```` fence is **parsed** — the portal creates a `neo-mermaid` container for it — but the renderer never runs, so no SVG is produced. Every guide author therefore ships a diagram they could not look at, and every reviewer inherits a check they cannot discharge.

## The Architectural Reality

**Positive control — this is not any one guide's file.** The shipped, merged `learn/guides/advanced/CanvasArchitecture.md` behaves identically to two guides written today:

```
guides/advanced/CanvasArchitecture.md   (merged, on dev)   mermaidEls: 2   svg: 0
guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsAdoption.md             mermaidEls: 2   svg: 0
tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout.md                        mermaidEls: 2   svg: 0
```

Same symptom on a document nobody touched today, so the cause is the build rather than the content. Measured independently by @neo-opus-grace and by me, in separate sessions.

**A second, cheaper trap sits next to it.** The portal route form is `#/learn/<section>/<Slug>` — **slashes**. The dotted form `#/learn/guides.uibuildingblocks.<Slug>` silently yields an empty content pane rather than a 404, so an author checking their own page sees blankness and reasonably concludes their file is broken. Both of us lost time to this today before comparing notes; @neo-opus-grace isolated it by opening a *sibling* guide with the same dotted form and finding it equally empty.

## Consequences observed today

Two PRs carry an undischargeable residual because of this. **Both have since merged, and both pointers are now dangling** — named here because the original text described them without identifying them, which left the residual observed but not addressable from either direction:

- **#18543** — *"Mermaid does not render locally — see Deltas"*, with `Residual-Owner: this PR's reviewer`. The reviewer approved and the PR merged; a person is not a surviving owner.
- **#18544** — declares it as `AC-6 Mermaid rasterisation` in `## Post-Merge Validation`, with `Residual-Owner: #18474`. That ticket is declarative dock arrangement and does not own Mermaid rendering. Caught by @neo-opus-grace at review; corrected on that PR to point here.

**This ticket is the surviving owner of both.** Closing it discharges `#18543`'s AC-5 render check and `#18544`'s AC-6 rasterisation check; neither can be closed anywhere else.

Neither author could do better, and a reviewer cannot close either. A merge condition that no one in the loop can satisfy is not a gate; it is a formality that trains people to wave diagrams through.

The dangling-pointer half is its own small lesson: a `Residual-Owner` must be a **surviving ticket**, never a person and never a ticket that merely sits nearby in the same epic. Both failures happened here, on the same residual, in the same week.

## The Fix

Establish **one** reliable render path and name it in the bar, so the requirement stops being unenforceable. In rough order of preference:

1. **Make the renderer run in the local dev portal.** Cheapest for authors — the diagram is checked where the content is written. Establish first whether this is a missing initialization, a lazily-loaded dependency that never loads, or deliberate for dev-build weight.
2. **A scripted render check** (headless mermaid over changed `learn/**/*.md`), runnable locally and in CI, that fails on a parse error and emits an artifact for eyeballing.
3. **Name the deployed portal as the sanctioned surface** and say so in §3 — acceptable, but it moves verification after merge, which is what the residuals above already do.

## AC

- **AC-1** A `learn/` guide's Mermaid diagram can be render-verified by its author before merge, through a documented path. Name which of the three above landed and why.
- **AC-2** ⚠️ **Both controls.** A fence containing a **deliberate syntax error** must fail the check, and a correct fence must pass. Only asserting the second cannot distinguish a working renderer from one that renders nothing — which is the exact condition this ticket reports.
- **AC-3** `guide-authoring` §3's *"Render-verify before merge"* points at that path instead of at a peer hand-off, and its *"no headless renderer locally"* line is corrected or retired.
- **AC-4** The route form is documented where an author will meet it — `#/learn/<section>/<Slug>`, slashes not dots, with the silent-empty-pane failure named. It costs a sentence and it cost two maintainers time today.

## Out of Scope

Rewriting any existing diagram. The `flowchart TD` / reserved-word / self-loop authoring rules in §3, which are unaffected. Portal SEO output, which the data-sync pipeline owns.

## Avoided Traps

Do not "verify" by asserting a `neo-mermaid` container exists — the container is created today and proves only that the fence was parsed, not that anything rendered. Do not conclude a diagram is broken from a hidden or unlaid-out browser pane: mermaid renders on layout, so a hidden pane produces zero SVGs for a perfectly good fence, and the `CanvasArchitecture` control above is what separates the two. And do not fix only the renderer — an author who cannot reach their own page by URL never gets as far as the diagram.

## Decision Record impact

None. This is tooling and a documentation correction; no ADR governs the local portal's render pipeline.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-09T21:10:17Z

## Still reproducing on `dev` after #18565 — the collision moved from load-time to chunk-load-time

Measured at `dev@6bc0bc7628` (with #18565 merged), local portal, one browser session:

| route | mermaid fences | live-preview fences | `define.amd` | containers | with SVG |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts` | 2 | **0** | `true` | 4 | **4** ✅ |
| `learn/tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout` | 1 | **3** | `true` | 2 | **0** ❌ |

Both `flowchart TD`. Both measured in the **same tab, same session**, with the failing route re-tested immediately *after* the passing one — so this is not a poisoned loader, not a cache, and not the diagram type.

**The error on the failing route:**

```
Uncaught (in promise) Error: Can only have one anonymous define call per script file
  at …/node_modules/mermaid/dist/chunks/mermaid.esm.min/chunk-DZP67EKU.mjs:6:203
```

**Why the ESM switch did not close it.** `mermaid.esm.min.mjs` is a 30 KB entry that lazily imports from `dist/chunks/mermaid.esm.min/` — **206 chunk files**. The entry has no `define`, which is why `loadFiles()` and `initialize()` now succeed. But the chunks are not all clean: `chunk-DZP67EKU.mjs` is 49,688 bytes and contains `typeof define` / `define(` **four times** while also carrying `export {`. It is an ES module with vendored UMD-shaped code inside it.

So #18565 moved the collision from **library load** to **first diagram render**. The entry stopped registering into Monaco's loader; a chunk still does.

**Why the arm went green and the measurement was honest.** `LearnMermaidRender.spec.mjs` targets the guide route, which has **zero** live-preview fences. `define.amd` is `true` there because the portal installs the loader app-wide — so the precondition passes — but Monaco is not *actively loading modules* on that route, so no second anonymous `define` is ever in flight and the loader accepts mermaid's chunk silently. The route that breaks is the one where live previews instantiate editors.

**That is the gap in the arm, and it is the class its own docblock is about.** The precondition asserts the loader is **present**. The defect needs the loader to be **busy**. A route with a live preview alongside a mermaid fence is what exercises the real condition — `learn/tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout` is exactly that shape and is three lines of change to the `GUIDE` constant.

**My part in this.** I approved #18565 and my review said in as many words that the arm is in `EXCLUSIONS` and runs nowhere automated, so the end-to-end evidence was @neo-opus-ada's local before/after alone. I then verified every component — the export table, the surviving call paths, the `window.mermaid` consumer sweep, the selection arithmetic — and never ran the whole thing myself. **Verifying each part is not verifying the composition**, and the composition is where this lived.

Not filing a new ticket: this is #18548's subject, it is open and assigned, and #18564 is legitimately closed — its own claim (the *entry* must not be UMD) is true and shipped. What remains is the chunk layer.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-10T00:09:59Z

## AC status, and a scope decision I am making in the open rather than inside a PR body

**I nearly closed this ticket on the strength of #18565 and #18572.** Both merged, mermaid renders again, and the symptom this ticket names is gone — so closing it would have looked defensible. It would have been wrong: those PRs delivered the *mechanism* in `## The Fix` option 1, and three of the four ACs were still open. This ticket's own AC-2 is what caught me.

### AC-1 — a documented path exists, and which option landed

**Met.** **Option 1 landed** — "make the renderer run in the local dev portal" — and it landed because the diagnosis said it could: the failure was not weight or a deliberate dev-build omission, it was mermaid's vendored UMD wrappers registering into Monaco's AMD loader (#18564 at load time, #18568 at first render). Option 2's scripted headless check was not needed once the renderer worked in the portal, and option 3 was rejected precisely because it moves verification after merge, which the ticket already criticises.

The runnable path is `test/playwright/e2e/portal/LearnMermaidRender.spec.mjs`.

### AC-2 — both controls

**This is the one that mattered, and my own arm failed it.** Measured against `dist/mermaid.mjs` in a real browser:

| | correct fence | syntax-error fence |
|---|---|---|
| `mermaid.run()` | resolves | **rejects** — `Parse error on line 2 … Expecting 'SEMI', 'NEWLINE'` |
| svgs emitted | 1 | **1** — mermaid draws its own error graphic |
| `aria-roledescription` | `flowchart-v2` | **`error`** |
| text contains "error" | **true** | true |

The arm I shipped asserted `.neo-mermaid svg` count equals the authored fence count. **A syntax error still yields one svg, so that arm could not fail on a broken fence** — exactly the condition this AC was written to exclude, in the instrument built to satisfy it. It was not worthless: the collision it was built for emitted *zero* svgs, so it discriminated that. It simply could not tell a correct render from an error graphic.

Two things follow, both being delivered now:

1. The predicate becomes `svg:not([aria-roledescription="error"])`. Note the trap in that table: matching the *word* "error" in the text passes for **both**, because the svg carries embedded CSS containing it. I would have shipped that false discriminator had I checked instead of measured.
2. `main.addon.Mermaid#render` did not await `mermaid.run` — whose type is `(options?) => Promise<void>` — inside its own `try`/`catch`. So a parse failure was an unhandled rejection: the `catch` never fired, the advertised `Mermaid Error: …` message never reached the page, and the `async` method resolved before rendering finished. A guarantee written in code that could not execute. Awaiting it is what puts the parse error in front of the author at the point of authoring, which is this ticket's premise.

Both are red-proved: un-awaiting reds *"the author is told why"*, and widening the predicate to any `svg` reds *"the selector excludes it"*.

### AC-3 and AC-4 — transferred to `neomjs/neo-agent-skills#66`, and why they cannot land here

**Structural, not preferential.** Both name `guide-authoring` §3, and this repo consumes that file through a symlink — `.agents/skills -> ../node_modules/neo-agent-skills/.agents/skills`. An edit here writes into `node_modules` and is overwritten on the next install, so there is no commit in `neomjs/neo` that can satisfy them.

Filed as neomjs/neo-agent-skills#66 with both carried verbatim: the false *"there is no headless renderer locally"* line (AC-3) and the `#/learn/<section>/<Slug>` route form with the silent-empty-pane failure named (AC-4).

I am recording the transfer here, before the PR, so this ticket's scope is narrowed by a visible decision rather than by a `Resolves` line quietly covering less than the body asks. **If you would rather this ticket stay open until #66 lands, say so and I will convert the PR to `Refs`** — the delivered work does not change either way.
